title: Mushroom
text: “So why exactly is it that Naofumi-san is staying in Melromarc? I thought I’d heard the reason, but I wanted to double-check.”

“Well… to put it simply, I want to help and rebuild the lives of the people from Eclair-san’s territory who were hurt by the Waves. Part of that means tracking down the ones who got sold into slavery through slave traders and buying them back.”

“That sounds like an awful lot of trouble to go through. From where I’m standing now, doing that in this country seems pointless. And what about all the other people who are enslaved? Are you just abandoning them?”
“…Even a god couldn’t save everyone. Ah, right—in this world, we’re treated like gods, aren’t we?”
Ah, here comes Itsuki’s idealistic nonsense aimed at Father again, I thought. Nothing ever changes with this one. But then, to my surprise, Itsuki let out a small sigh.

“I spoke out of turn. You’re right. There’s no ally of justice in this world, so I suppose there’s no god either… no, if there were some all-powerful god just letting a world like this rot, I’d have to deal with him myself.”
“Well, it might not go that far, but if there is one, I doubt he’s a particularly good god.”
“…Even I’ve started thinking that it’d be enough just to protect the people within my own sight.”

Father’s attitude toward gods felt like something he’d genuinely believed even before coming to this world, I thought. He wants to believe, yet if such a being truly existed, he’d be the first to doubt it… Ark, I recalled, was said to harbor outright hatred for the concept of gods. Hou-kun had seemed much the same. I supposed that no matter how much power one wielded, thinking of the people who inevitably slipped through the cracks made it impossible to arrogantly call oneself a god.
“Come to think of it, there’s a reason you’re so ridiculously tough and strong, isn’t there, Naofumi-san? Would you mind telling me? I want to get stronger myself.”
“And what exactly do you intend to do with that strength?”
“First… well, for now, I want to atone for all the trouble I caused you.”
“Atone, huh…”
“I caused you that much trouble, after all. No matter how wrong I think you are about something, I’ll still take your side.”

Ho ho, so Itsuki has learned a bit of humility now that he’s faced reality. Well, since Father is inherently always in the right, I supposed we’d just have Itsuki work hard from now on with a properly reformed heart.
“Let’s hope it never comes to that. But that’s not what I meant—I’m asking about your own personal code of conduct, Itsuki.”

“That’s obvious, isn’t it… I’m going to do what I want to do. First, get Emia-san’s family back. Then make the ones who sold me pay, wipe out the scum torturing demi-humans and beastmen across this country, and finally head to Siltvelt to challenge the Waves. Heh… I’ll do the bare minimum required of a hero.”

Mole’s relatives were apparently gathering in Zeltoble sometime later. It seemed the conclusion had been reached that there wasn’t much demand for Mole’s kind in Melromarc. Anyway, Itsuki seemed to think he was smirking nihilistically just now, but honestly, Itsuki, you’re wearing a riska form, so the whole effect falls rather flat. Still, it looked like Itsuki had developed quite a thing for Mole. Ah, I see how it is. Normally Itsuki gets along fine with Riska, but perhaps due to the effects of going feral, he started longing for someone different—just like Father did back in the first world. After all, cherishing Big Sister above all else only really happens in the loop where she’s the first one purchased, just like in the original world. Otherwise, one just ends up as a guardian figure. Perhaps a similar shift was happening within Itsuki now. Best not to dwell on this line of thinking too much, though—I had a feeling Big Sister might beat me to death somewhere down the line if I did.
“That’s not quite as ‘do whatever I want’ as it sounded at first. Well, a sense of justice isn’t a bad thing, and it sounds like you’ve found a concrete purpose—doing something for someone else.”
Father was clearly thinking of Takt as he said this. Compared to that lot, Itsuki’s “what I want to do” did seem far less self-centered.
“That’s a bit of a relief, honestly. I think we just never meshed well before—Itsuki’s always been fundamentally decent, which is probably why he was chosen as a hero in the first place.”
“…If that’s what you think, then I suppose it must be true. In your world, anyway.”
“Ha ha… yeah, that’s what I think.”
“Well, Ren will probably teach him anyway, and it’d be good if he could learn it too if possible… Anyway, Itsuki, let’s get along from here on out.”

“Whether we ‘get along’ or not is a separate matter, but our goals overlap somewhat, so I’ll cooperate with you. It’s better for Emia-san’s mental state to be left in your care too. That said, if you ever try selling her off, I’ll kill you.”

“I wouldn’t do that… besides, I’ve already got the children and others entrusted somewhere else, somewhere peaceful, separate from here. It’d probably be best for Emia-san to go along with Imiya-chan, don’t you think?”

And so, it seemed Itsuki would be cooperating with us. Once he heard from Father about how to strengthen weapons, he managed to put it into practice that very same day—faster than even Ren had. Apparently, thanks to Mole’s influence, some of Father’s own desires as Shield Hero had bled into it, or something like that.
“Um… could you please get off my back sometime soon?”

Itsuki had been talking this whole time while still riding on Rabbit Guy’s back. Rabbit Guy was sweating bullets. Itsuki kept yanking on his ears and stomping his back with a satisfied ka-thunk, ka-thunk.
“Ah, right, sorry about that. My apologies for the trouble. As an apology, let me offer you one of my prized ingredients.”
“Do you even understand what an apology is supposed to look like!?”
With practiced ease, Itsuki reached a hand right into his own mouth and pulled a poisonous mushroom out of his cheek pouch. Disgusting. Don’t hand someone something you just had in your mouth, I say.
“Here, have this delicious mushroom, and go keep Rishia-san company for a while. She loves stories, you know. And since you seem like the reading type yourself, I imagine you two would get along.”

Itsuki was doing something bafflingly pointless. Somehow it felt like one of Father’s jokes? It reminded me of how Big Sister sometimes laments that Father says odd things completely deadpan or gets carried away with a bit too much enthusiasm.
“That’s a poison mushroom, isn’t it!? I don’t want it! And why on earth would you pull it out of your mouth in the first place!?”

Rabbit Guy apparently recognized it instantly from something he’d read. Well, it was obvious enough—bright red cap, unmistakably poisonous at a glance. A toxic mushroom resembling a fly agaric. If I recalled correctly, it was called something like Scarlet Death Meat Spore. A versatile ingredient used in all sorts of compounding, including as a base material for Ouroboros’s deadly poison—one of the more basic toxins out there.

“If it were poisonous, there’s no way I’d eat it—I always properly appraise things before eating! And it’s delicious, besides. It even has restorative properties that leave you brimming with energy for a while.”

Itsuki chomped down and started munching away on the poison mushroom. He kept eating away happily as if to prove it wasn’t poison at all, but Rabbit Guy adamantly refused, insisting there was absolutely no way he’d try it.
“No… Itsuki, that’s poison. My weapon literally shows it as poison.”
“Same here. Itsuki, are you okay? Did the torture mess with your head that badly?”
“No, that shouldn’t be… though it is strange that neither Emia-san nor Rishia-san ever eat these…”
“Ah, right, I think there was some research showing that riska can eat poisonous mushrooms without any issue.”
Now that I thought about it, I did recall riska having some default ability that let them eat any kind of mushroom.
“It’s a Riska-species trait. You already know about the wall-climbing and such, don’t you?”
Rafumi appeared out of nowhere to explain this to Itsuki. Right after, Itsuki fired off an arrow at her, only for it to be dodged with a soft poof.
“An afterimage… still not enough training, I see.”
“Please stop appearing out of nowhere for no reason. It’s unpleasant.”
“Heh, I only told you because you clearly didn’t know.”
“All you ever do is say unnecessary things, you!”
“Now, now… anyway, Itsuki, it seems you’re the only one who can eat poison mushrooms, so just accept that, okay?”
“Can’t be helped, I suppose. But really, this mushroom is genuinely delicious. Oh, I have another kind too.”
This time, Itsuki pulled out a spotted mushroom.
